Question: What are some amazing facts about airplanes?
Answer: 1.When a plane lands at night, cabin crews will dim the interior lights because in the unlikely event that the plane landing goes badly and passengers need to evacuate, their eyes will already be adjusted to the darkness. 2.Only 5% of the world’s population had ever been on an airplane till 2013 which drastically increased to approx. 20 percent in 2020. 3.A Boeing 747 is made up of six million parts which are made to be all controlled by a few pilots sitting up front with switches and buttons under their fingertips. 4.It is the rule that pilots must be fed the same multi-course meal given to those in the first and business class whilst the co-pilots are encouraged to eat different entrees to guard against cases of food poisoning. 5.Those white lines that planes leave in the sky are simply trails of condensation, hence their technical name of “contrails.” Plane engines release water vapor as part of the combustion process. When that hot water vapor is pumped out of the exhaust and hits the cooler air of the upper atmosphere, it creates those puffy white lines in the sky. It’s basically the same reaction as when you see your breath when it’s cold outside. 6.Environment inside an airplane actually alters the way food and drink tastes—sweet items tasted less sweet, while salty flavors were heightened. The dry recycled air inside the plane cabin doesn’t help either as low humidity can further dull taste and smell making everything in a plane seem bland. 7.Plane doors can't actually open in mid-flight. 8.Australian airline Qantas has never had a fatal accident involving one of its commercial aircrafts. 9.The fastest commercial plane flew at twice the speed of sound. It was the Concorde, that regularly flew over the Atlantic, and was decommissioned after an accident involving Concorde, in France. 10.Long-haul flights have secret bedrooms and a bathroom for flight attendants. 11.Living in an airplane flight path could harm your heart.Means closer to the airport.Individuals exposed to noise above 60 decibels on a regular basis—like the sound of an airplane overhead—had a 30 percent greater risk of dying from a heart attack than those typically exposed to noise levels under 45 decibels. 12.Research shows that the first 3 minutes after takeoff and the final 8 minutes before landing are when 80% of plane crashes happen. 13.About 1 in 5 people have some form of fear of flying, or “aviophobia.” 14.If you sit at the back of an airplane, your odds of surviving a crash are 40% higher. 15.What that tiny hole in the airplane window does is to regulate cabin pressure. Most airplane windows are made up of three panels of acrylic. The exterior window works as you would expect—keeping the elements out and maintaining cabin pressure. 16.Airplanes are designed to withstand lightning strikes. Question: Can you tell me something inspiring?
Answer: Vikram Batra,one of the bravehearts of Indian Army. He fought for India in the Kargil War and lost his life at the age of 24 for the nation. Let me take you through his life story. First I would like to mention about his love story and how much he cared about Dimple Mam(his love) The couple used to be apart a lot because of Batra’s mission and whenever she used to get pressurised for getting married, he would always tell her, “Take care of what you like, or you will be forced to like what you get.” It was a ritual for the couple to visit the Mansa Devi temple and Gurudwara Sri Nada Sahab. During one such visit, while doing parikrama, he was holding her dupatta and on completing the parikrama said, “Congratulations, Mrs Batra!” On one of his next visits, when Dimple raised her concern of marriage, he took a blade out of his wallet, cut his thumb and filled her ‘maang’ with his blood. Under his leadership, the platoon successfully cleared three of the four bunkers but while clearing the fourth bunker, a grenade from the enemy’s side fell directly on Captain Nayyar. Despite being severely injured, he continued to lead the remaining men in his company. It was only after clearing the last bunker that he breathed his last on 7 July, 1999. On the other hand amid thick fog, Captain Batra and his men set out to climb to the top of the peak 4875 (approx 16,000 feet high) not worrying about the enemy firing with a heavy machine gun from the top. This strategic point was crucial to India's major push to regain dominance in the regions occupied by the Pakistani military forces. Captain Batra valiantly led his troops and fought the infiltrating Pakistani army tooth and tail. From braving bullets to physical blows, he commanded a team of exemplary bravehearts. However, Batra ran out of luck when he was faced by a machine gun nest manned by a Pakistani army man. Such was his nobility, he asked the Subedar with him to take a step back because he had a family and took the lead. He braved the enemy bullets but a stray splinter from a rocket-propelled grenade hit Captain Batra in the head and he collapsed immediately. At last every Indian knows the slogan that Sher Shah(Vikram Batra codename) used to say The heart wants more. Captain Vikram Batra received the Paramvir Chakra while Captain Anuj Nayyar received Mahavir Chakra for their bravery.
